question: In ΔPQR, , if 4∠P = 5∠Q = 20∠R, then the value of ∠Q is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let 4∠P = 5∠Q = 20∠R = LCM(4, 5, 20) = 20.

⇒ ∠P : ∠Q : ∠R = 20/4 : 20/5 : 20/20 = 5 : 4 : 1

The sum of all angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ Total parts = 5 + 4 + 1 = 10 parts = 180° ⇒ 1 part = 18°

⇒ ∠Q = 4 parts = 4 × 18° = 72°

**∴ The correct answer is 72°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In ΔPQR, 4∠P = 5∠Q = 20∠R

**Formula Used:**

The sum of all internal angles of a triangle is always 180°.

∠P + ∠Q + ∠R = 180°

 

 

 

 

 
 P
 Q
 R
 
 90°
 72°
 18°

**Calculations:**

Let 4∠P = 5∠Q = 20∠R = k

⇒ ∠P = k/4

⇒ ∠Q = k/5

⇒ ∠R = k/20

Substituting these values into the angle sum property of a triangle:

⇒ k/4 + k/5 + k/20 = 180°

Taking the LCM of the denominators (4, 5, 20) which is 20:

⇒ (5k + 4k + k) ÷ 20 = 180°

⇒ 10k ÷ 20 = 180°

⇒ k / 2 = 180°

⇒ k = 360°

Now, substitute the value of k back into the expression for ∠Q:

⇒ ∠Q = 360° ÷ 5

⇒ ∠Q = 72°

**∴ The correct answer is 72°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Angles Property

The sum of the three interior angles of any planar triangle is always exactly 180°. (∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°)

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote and non-adjacent interior angles.

Types of Triangles Based on Angles

If all angles are less than 90°, it is an acute triangle. If one angle is exactly 90°, it is a right-angled triangle. If one angle is greater than 90°, it is an obtuse triangle.
